review.headline: A clean, punishing tactical win over an overextended Sicilian

sections.text: You played a textbook Open Sicilian where Black simplified early with 4...Nxd4, letting you plant your queen comfortably on d4. You developed smoothly with 6.Be2, 7.O-O, and 8.Nd2, keeping your pieces coordinated while Black set up on the flanks.

Black lost patience with 10...e5??, leaving their central pawn undefended. You punished it immediately with 11.Qxe5+!, winning a pawn and seizing control of the e-file. After 11...Be7, you kept the pressure on with 12.Ba3, targeting the pinned piece.

Under heavy fire, Black blundered a full bishop with 12...O-O??. You scooped it up via 13.Qxe7 Qxe7 14.Bxe7, traded down into a winning endgame, and capped it off cleanly when 21.Bf3 picked up the rook with 22.Bxa8.

review.turning_point: Black's 10...e5?? blundered a critical center pawn to 11.Qxe5+!, cracking open their position and leading directly to their collapse.
review.focus: Your conversion was flawless—keep playing sharp, alert chess like 11.Qxe5+ when your opponent weakens their center.

review.headline: A rock-solid Petrov performance decided on the clock

sections.text: You handled the opening with great discipline. In the Petrov's Defense, after 5.Bc4 d5 6.Bb3 Nf6, you seized space in the center, developed naturally with 7...Bg4 and 8...Be7, and castled without any issues. By move 12, you had completely equalized.

Your only slight misstep came on move 14 with 14...Bg6?!, allowing White to compromise your pawn structure with 15.Bxg6 fxg6. While keeping your bishop active with 14...Bg5 was cleaner, you quickly stabilized the position. You applied pressure on the queenside with 16...Qb6 and smoothly traded queens with 17...Qxb3.

The endgame transition was clinically played. After exchanging rooks through 20...Rxe2 and 22...Rf8, you rerouted your knight with 23...Nxf8 and 24...Ne6, culminating in the active 26...Nd3 to hit the b2-pawn. Facing mounting positional pressure, White ran out of time.

review.turning_point: White's time expired right as your knight invaded with 26...Nd3, targeting the weak b2-pawn and seizing the initiative in the minor-piece endgame.
review.focus: Be careful about inviting doubled pawns without concrete compensation, as seen with 14...Bg6 instead of maintaining piece tension with 14...Bg5.
